title: Internal pentest from the company jump box
summary: On an authorized internal test the team works from the jump box the company issued for it, over SSH, and keeps everything it collects on a separate Linux computer. A Jenkins server exposes a service account that turns out to administer the server VLAN, and the lead holds for the champion before anyone uses it.

findings.claim: Anyone on the server VLAN can read a Jenkins job that holds a current domain password in plain text.
That password belongs to svc-build, which administers every server in 10.20.2.0/24 through Server Admins.

messages.text:
**M-0021 is open: internal pentest of the ACME server VLAN.** @Lunar Fox leads.

Work only from **ACME Jump Box**; it is the box ACME issued for this test. Scope is 10.20.0.0/22. No denial of service, and clear anything that signs in as someone with me first.

Plan: @Clever Heron sweeps the VLAN from the jump box, @Quiet Lynx takes whatever web services turn up, and @Silver Kite looks at identity once we have names. Anything we collect goes to **Analysis**; nothing is kept on ACME's box.

Sweep done from **ACME Jump Box**:

```
$ nmap -sV --top-ports 200 10.20.0.0/22 -oA vlan
61 hosts up
10.20.1.15   8080/tcp  http  Jetty (Jenkins 2.387)
...
14 hosts: SMB signing enabled but not required
```

The Jenkins stands out. Copied `vlan.xml` to Analysis and removed it from the jump box.

Jenkins lets anonymous users read job configs. One of them, `deploy-intranet`, sets a password in its shell step:

```
$ curl -s http://10.20.1.15:8080/job/deploy-intranet/config.xml | grep -n SVC
41:  export SVC_USER=svc-build
42:  export SVC_PASS='Wi••••••••••26'
```

Read only: no builds triggered, nothing changed. Pulled all 24 configs to **Analysis**; the other 23 hold no secrets.

One LDAP bind from the jump box, nothing else:

```
$ ldapwhoami -H ldap://dc01 -D svc-build -w ••••
u:CORP\svc-build
$ ldapsearch ... '(sAMAccountName=svc-build)' memberOf
memberOf: CN=Server Admins,OU=Groups,DC=corp,DC=acme,DC=example
```

The password is current, and Server Admins is local admin on every host in 10.20.2.0/24. I have not signed in anywhere with it.

@Dana Okafor, where we are: an anonymous Jenkins page hands out **svc-build**, and svc-build administers the whole server subnet. Severity is high.

To prove the reach I would like to sign in as svc-build on two servers you choose and list the local administrators, read-only, from the jump box. Holding until you say go.
